title: Pulsed single-photon magnetometry with a $Λ$-type three-level system: near-optimal frequency-resolved photon counting
authors: Seyed Mostafa Moniri, Elnaz Darsheshdar, Mikayel Khanbekyan
abstract: We investigate pulsed single-photon magnetometry with a Zeeman-sensitive $Λ$-type three-level system driven by a classical control field. We derive the asymptotic output state and decompose its quantum Fisher information into photon-loss, spectral-intensity, and spectral-phase contributions. Environmental coupling reshapes the scattering response and can increase magnetic-field information. At critical coupling, real-frequency zeros of the scattering amplitude redistribute information toward measurable spectral intensity, allowing frequency-resolved photon counting to capture nearly all of the magnetic-field information encoded in the output state when the zeros lie within the pulse bandwidth. For long Gaussian pulses with a smooth, nonzero central-frequency scattering amplitude, the additional spectral-intensity contribution and residual spectral-phase information gap decrease as $T^{-2}$ or faster.
summary: The paper investigates single-photon magnetometry using a $\Lambda$-system, comparing information extraction from photon loss versus frequency-resolved photon counting. It shows that environmental coupling can enhance sensitivity, and crucially, at critical coupling, frequency-resolved counting can approach the ultimate quantum limit by accessing information previously hidden in the spectral phase.
main_problem: To determine if frequency-resolved photon counting can extract magnetic-field information from a single-photon scattering process in a $\Lambda$-type three-level system, potentially surpassing the limits set by simple photon-loss measurements.
main_result: Frequency-resolved photon counting can capture nearly all the magnetic-field information encoded in the output state, especially at critical coupling where scattering amplitude zeros redistribute information to measurable spectral intensity.
method: The analysis involves deriving the asymptotic output state and decomposing the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) into classical (photon-loss) and quantum (spectral-intensity/phase) contributions.
model_or_system: The system is a Zeeman-sensitive $\Lambda$-type three-level atom probed by a single-photon pulse and driven by a classical control field. The dynamics are analyzed using the Hamiltonian in the rotating frame, incorporating environmental coupling.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), frequency-resolved Correlation Function of Intensity ($C_\omega(pB)$), spectral intensity, and spectral phase.
important_parameters: Environmental coupling rates ($\Gamma_g, \Gamma_\perp$), detunings ($\Delta_g, \delta$), and the ratio $\Gamma_\perp/\Gamma_g$ (especially at critical coupling).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting spontaneous branching from $|eangle	o |sangle$ and lower-state coherence dephasing, and analyzing the long-pulse limit using Gaussian pulse profiles.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the magnetometry setup, the spectral densities of the output fields at different magnetic fields, and the frequency-resolved CFI plotted against the ratio of coupling rates ($\Gamma_\perp/\Gamma_g$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by setting up the physical model and Hamiltonian, deriving the asymptotic output state, decomposing the QFI, and then analyzing the specific measurement scheme of frequency-resolved photon counting, culminating in the comparison between the achievable CFI and the theoretical QFI.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for quantum sensing using cavity/atomic systems, specifically quantifying how different measurement observables (loss vs. spectral intensity) relate to the fundamental quantum limits (QFI) in the presence of environmental coupling.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic of pulsed single-photon magnetometry with a Zeeman-sensitive Λ-type three-level system. An incident single-photon pulse couples the |g⟩↔|e⟩transition at rate Γg, while a classical control field with Rabi frequency Ωc drives the |s⟩↔|e⟩transition. The magnetic field modifies the one-photon detuning ∆g and the two-photon detuning δ. Emission into environmental modes is described by Γ⊥.

Figure 2. Magnetic-field and pulse-duration dependence for the 40Ca+ value rZ = 0.76 at critical coupling Γ⊥= Γg, with Ωc/Γg = 1 and δ0 = ∆g,0 = 0. (a) Total output-state QFI Q(ρxB), frequency-resolved CFI Cω(pxB), and photon-loss CFI C(pxB) versus xB for ΓgT = 2. (b) The same quantities versus ΓgT at xB = 0.3. The inset shows the information gap Q −Cω on log-log axes together with a T −2 reference dependence; the numerical data follow the predicted asymptotic scaling at large T.

Figure 3. Information redistribution as a function of the normalized environmental coupling rate Γ⊥/Γg for rZ = 0.76, xB = 0.3, ΓgT = 2, Ωc/Γg = 1, and δ0 = ∆g,0 = 0. (a) Total QFI Q, frequency-resolved CFI Cω, and photon-loss CFI C. The blue vertical line marks critical coupling, Γ⊥/Γg = 1, while the second vertical line marks the QFI maximum at Γ⊥/Γg ≃1.34. (b) Exact decomposition into photon-loss information C, additional spectral-intensity information Cω −C, and residual spectral-phase information Q −Cω.

Figure 4. Incident spectral density |˜ξ(ω)|2 and output spectral density |uB(ω)|2 at critical coupling Γ⊥= Γg, for rZ = 0.76, ΓgT = 2, Ωc/Γg = 1, and δ0 = ∆g,0 = 0. The panels correspond to (a) xB = 0, (b) xB = 0.3, (c) xB = 0.574, and (d) xB = 0.8. Vertical dashed lines mark the analytical scattering-zero positions ω(0) ± . In panel (c), one zero lies at the pulse center.

Figure 5. Frequency-resolved CFI Cω(pxB) versus Γ⊥/Γg for Ωc/Γg = 0.5, 1, 2, 4, using rZ = 0.76, xB = 0.3, ΓgT = 2, and δ0 = ∆g,0 = 0. The vertical dashed line marks critical coupling, Γ⊥= Γg. The critical feature is pronounced for weak and moderate control and becomes suppressed when the scattering zeros move away from the incident pulse bandwidth.
